identity.notes: admiralspalast.de (the venue's naive domain) 301-redirects to atgentertainment.de, the operator group's corporate site, not this venue's own presence — that redirect target was rejected as the official_url for exactly that reason. admiralspalast.theater is the venue's own dedicated first-party domain: its retained <title> is 'Admiralspalast, Berlin', its homepage meta description names the venue directly ('Im Admiralspalast Berlin erwartet das Publikum ein vielfältiges Live-Programm...'), and every sampled event detail page repeats the identical retained address block 'Admiralspalast Berlin / Friedrichstr. 101 / 10117 Berlin' — consistent with the venue's well-known real-world address in Mitte, Berlin.

site_classification.platform: Contao Open Source CMS (retained <meta name="generator" content="Contao Open Source CMS"> on every sampled page). No JSON-LD Event data, no ICS/iCal link, no WordPress signals (no wp-content/wp-json), no Fourvenues script, no Sanity config — event data is exposed only as static, semantically-classed server-rendered HTML (event list cards + per-event 'Termine & Tickets' blocks with dedicated evDay/evMJ/evWdT spans).

start_date.notes: The event detail page's 'Termine & Tickets' item row does not state one single combined date string. It states the day-of-month and the month+year in two separate sibling spans within the SAME event row (not inherited from a distant page-level heading shared across unrelated events): 01 and Nov 2026. Concatenating them mechanically yields 2026-11-01 with no other possible reading, since both spans are scoped to this one event's own row.

derivation.rule: Within one '.item' event row on an event's own detail page, the 'evDay' span (day-of-month) and 'evMJ' span (3-letter month abbreviation + 4-digit year) are sibling elements describing that single event only. Map the 3-letter month abbreviation to its numeric month (standard German/English abbreviation, e.g. 'Nov' -> 11) and concatenate as <evMJ year>-<evMJ month, zero-padded>-<evDay, zero-padded>. Exactly one row's worth of spans is being combined, never a page-wide heading shared across multiple different events.

time.notes: The same event row's own So, 20:00 states the local time-of-day directly as a literal substring ('20:00') of one retained element — no combination with a separate element needed. No UTC offset or IANA timezone is stated anywhere on the page, so this is honestly a floating local time, not upgraded to a UTC instant.

end.notes: No end time or end date is exposed anywhere on the retained event-list or event-detail pages for the sampled event.

venue_location.notes: This is a single-venue site (unlike e.g. Razzmatazz's multiple numbered rooms) — every sampled event detail page carries the identical retained 'Adresse Theater' address block naming the venue and its full postal address directly, on the same page as the event's own date/time data. No cross-page or cross-section combination is needed.

source_record_id.notes: No numeric id is exposed on the venue's own pages. Each event's own detail-page URL slug ('/veranstaltung/{slug}.html') is this source's own permanent, source-authored path for that event, directly stated as the href on every list card and reused as the canonical URL of the detail page itself — the same documented URL-slug-as-source_record_id strategy already established for moog-barcelona-01 and LAV (ingestion/lav/discovery.mjs).

event_url.notes: Each event card's own href, directly stated, and independently confirmed by fetching it (HTTP 200, ev-event-detail).

price.notes: No price is stated on the venue's own event list or detail pages for the sampled event. The detail page's own 'Tickets' button links out to a third-party ticketing site (eventim.de) where price presumably appears — that is Eventim's own page, not this source's own first-party data, and was not treated as this source's price per the policy's third-party-authority rule.

blockers.description: Only one real event (Cem Adrian) was sampled at detail-page granularity. A full month-abbreviation mapping table (Jan/Feb/Mär/Apr/Mai/Jun/Jul/Aug/Sep/Okt/Nov/Dez) would need to be built and exercised against a handful more sampled events before an offline parser could be trusted across the whole event-list page — not yet proven for months other than 'Nov'.
No explicit UTC offset or IANA timezone is stated on any retained page; 'time' is honestly a floating local (presumed Europe/Berlin) time, not a proven UTC instant.

reasons: Identity PROVEN from the venue's own dedicated first-party domain (admiralspalast.theater), not the operator-group redirect target.

A CONFIRMED public data path retained for both the event-list page and one real event-detail page.
title PROVEN (DIRECT_SOURCE) and start_date PROVEN (DETERMINISTIC_CONTEXT, combining two sibling spans within one event's own row, no page-wide heading inheritance).
source_record_id PROVEN via a documented URL-slug strategy, matching the moog-barcelona-01/LAV precedent.
recommended_family STATIC_EVENT_LIST, an existing documented reusable family — no new collector family required.

Not advanced to READY_FOR_ACTIVATION: no DETERMINISTIC_DERIVATION evidence item has been produced in this investigation (no offline parser/test was written), which the v1.2 activation gates require for the start_date field's DETERMINISTIC_CONTEXT basis — that offline-proof/collector-wiring step is deliberately left as separate follow-up work, per this task's own instructions.
